area: data model (Prisma schema → target PostgreSQL schema for FastAPI)
summary: The repo root is C:\projects\kidsphere. prisma/schema.prisma (907 lines) defines 36 models and 23 Postgres enum types, built for a multi-tenant platform. Every child table carries organizationId. It has a 5-role hierarchy and a questionnaire engine (ParentQuestionnaire/ParentResponse). It also has an evidence-based attribute engine (ProfileAttribute + Evidence + ConfidenceLevel), goals with evidence, interventions, outcomes and class weekly plans. Content is versioned with an approval log (ContentAsset/Version/Approval/Template), plus family-photo media with consent, teacher audio narration, child-device sessions, notifications, parent messages and AI/analytics/audit logs. There are 3 Prisma migrations (20261004215311_init with 917 lines, plus two one-column ALTERs). prisma/seed.ts builds a 2-tenant demo through the TS services, and its Adam story matches spec §44. src/lib/db.ts is only a Prisma singleton. About 9 of the 36 models map onto the spec §28 tables, after heavy simplification. Users/Session, the class-based teacher scope, parent links and AuditLog cover §34/§35 needs that §28 leaves out, so they stay as 6 small supporting tables. Everything else is outside the MVP. Production kidsphere_app holds only an admin user and one empty Organization, so no data needs porting. The plan is a fresh schema of 15 tables (9 spec + 6 supporting) using UUID keys, TEXT+CHECK instead of PG enums, and JSONB for profile and content shapes. Migrations should be hand-written Alembic revisions applied on the Ubuntu server.

Keep the rule that AI suggestions never activate anything without teacher approval.

simplify.reason: The §4–§11 wizard is a fixed 7-step form. One row per answer plus status/version tables is engine overhead.

simplify.reason: §28: content_type story|video|digital_game|real_world_activity; status draft|approved|completed|archived; mode strength_builder|growth_support.

MOVEMENT, ROLE_PLAY, TEACHER_DISCUSSION and PARENT_HOME → real_world_activity. VISUAL_ROUTINE is dropped. WEEKLY_PLAN becomes a pack_id grouping. TEACHER_REVIEW is dropped. simplify.item: Observation QUICK/FULL + ObservationDomain + ObservationItem → one observations table
simplify.reason: §21 needs a single quick observation (under 30 s). The full domain checklist with 4-level ratings is out of the MVP loop.
simplify.how: ObservationKind becomes observations.source (quick|content_feedback). The ObservationDomain join becomes one area TEXT column, with DevelopmentDomain keys reused as values. ObservationRating is replaced by functional_level independent|with_support|difficult, plus support_level none|some|significant. simplify.reason: §11's parent priority list (Emotional, Social, Language, Communication, Independence, Attention, Motor, Learning, Transitions, Confidence, Other) differs slightly from the current 11 domains.

simplify.item: Postgres enum types → TEXT + CHECK; cuid → UUID
simplify.reason: Native enums are awkward to evolve: values cannot be removed or renamed easily, and enum DDL is fiddly in Alembic. cuid() was Prisma-side generation.
simplify.how: Every status/role/type column becomes TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (col IN (...)), validated again with Pydantic Literal. Primary keys use uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() (built into PG16). Timestamps are timestamptz DEFAULT now().

simplify.reason: The same idea (one shared client) is needed in Python. The server has about 1.4 GB RAM free.
simplify.how: One SQLAlchemy 2.0 engine (psycopg 3 driver, pool_size≈5, max_overflow≈5) plus a get_db() FastAPI dependency yielding a Session per request. No repository layer.

add.item: Target schema: 15 tables (9 from §28 + 6 supporting)
add.reason: Covers §28 plus the §34/§35 needs (auth sessions, classes, assignment, parent links, audit) without approaching '50 tables'.

The timeline then reads one table.

add.reason: §23–§25: AI-drafted current understanding needs teacher approval, plus baseline validation and per-focus review. Nothing like this exists today.

Only on approval does the summary copy into child_profiles.current_understanding, satisfying §27's teacher-in-control rule.

add.item: Migration tooling: Alembic with hand-written revisions, run on the server
add.reason: There is no local Python, so everything runs on Ubuntu. Alembic gives a version table, transactional DDL on PG and upgrade/downgrade from the venv with one command, which is less to build than a home-made SQL runner. Autogenerate needs a live DB comparison, so it is unreliable here.
add.how: pip install alembic, sqlalchemy>=2 and psycopg[binary]. Write 0001_initial by hand, using op.create_table or op.execute of reviewed SQL, with CHECK constraints spelled out. Deploy step: `sudo -u kidsphere /var/www/kidsphere/backend/venv/bin/alembic upgrade head`. If the team chooses raw psycopg without SQLAlchemy, numbered .sql files plus a schema_migrations table applied with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -1 -f` is the equally valid fallback; pick one, not both.

add.item: Prod cutover + admin bootstrap
add.reason: kidsphere_app holds only an admin user and one empty organization, so nothing needs migrating. A clean DB avoids leftover Prisma enum types and _prisma_migrations.
add.how: 1) `sudo -u postgres pg_dump -Fc kidsphere_app > /root/kidsphere_app-pre-fastapi.dump`. 2) Create a new DB (e.g. kidsphere, owner kidsphere, UTF8) and run `alembic upgrade head`. Leave kidsphere_app untouched until nginx is switched, then drop it later. 3) Create the admin with a `python -m app.cli create-admin` command, which prompts for the password on the server, or copy email/name/password_hash from the old User row. 4) Create one kindergarten and one class in the admin UI.

add.item: Staging/test databases on the server
add.reason: Migrations and pytest cannot run locally.
add.how: Create kidsphere_test (pytest, recreated per run) and optionally kidsphere_staging on the same PG16. Dry-run `alembic upgrade head && alembic downgrade base && alembic upgrade head` there before each prod deploy.

risks: No local Python or Postgres: every migration and data-model test runs only on the server. A bad revision fails at deploy time, so dry-run on kidsphere_test/staging first and keep a pg_dump before each prod upgrade.

JSONB shape drift: without per-column Pydantic models and a schema_version key, child_profiles and baseline_data fields will diverge between wizard versions. Never trust JSONB read back without validation.

Provenance loss: dropping ProfileAttributeEvidence means 'who entered each piece' (§12) survives only if every JSONB item and baseline section carries source/added_by/added_at. This has to be built in from the first migration.
The baseline 'never overwrite' rule is app-enforced unless the optional UPDATE-blocking trigger is added. Without the trigger, a careless PUT route could break §3/§12.
Max-3-active focus areas: the current goal check (src/server/services/goals.ts:20) is count-then-insert and racy. The new service must lock the child row (or use a trigger).

Login identifier: src/server/validators/index.ts loginSchema accepts a plain username such as 'admin'. If the prod admin's email field is not a real address, a Pydantic EmailStr on users.email or the login form will lock them out. Use a plain lower-cased str.
Password hashes: use the `bcrypt` package. passlib is unmaintained and breaks with bcrypt>=4.1. bcryptjs $2a$/$2b$ hashes are then verifiable if the old admin row is copied.

Collation: deploy/install.sh:55 creates DBs with LC_COLLATE 'C', so Hebrew/Arabic names sort by code point. For the new DB, consider C.UTF-8 or ORDER BY name COLLATE "und-x-icu" (Ubuntu PG16 ships ICU).

Spec literal vs model: §28 has children.kindergarten as a column, but §34 needs admin-managed classes and teacher assignment. The recommendation (class_id FK + kindergartens/classes/class_teachers) deviates from the literal table list. Confirm with the product owner that 6 supporting tables are acceptable.
Feedback double-write: content_feedback, the mirrored observation and the content status change must happen in one transaction, or the timeline and content status disagree.

Path and name mismatch: production currently uses DB/role kidsphere_app, /opt/kidsphere-app, /var/lib/kidsphere-app/storage and port 3070 (deploy/deploy-kids.ps1). Spec §47 mandates /var/www/kidsphere/{frontend,backend,uploads}. Decide the DB and role names up front so .env, the systemd unit and the backup scripts agree.

Parent visibility: parents must see only generated_content that is shared_with_parent and approved/completed. Observations, reviews and the profile's health/internal sections must never come through parent endpoints. This is easy to regress without porting the security.test.ts scenarios.

area: Server business logic, auth, permissions, privacy (src/server/services, src/server/validators, src/lib/auth, src/lib/permissions, src/lib/audit, errors/route/env/mailer/storage, child-session, proxy.ts, src/features/auth, src/features/admin)
summary: Auth uses bcrypt through bcryptjs 3.0.3 at cost 12 (src/lib/auth/password.ts). Hashes look like `$2b$12$…`, are 60 characters, are computed over the UTF-8 password and silently truncate past 72 bytes. Sessions are opaque and stored in the database, not JWTs. A 32-byte random base64url token sits in the httpOnly cookie `ks_session` (SameSite=Lax, Secure when COOKIE_SECURE=true, 7-day TTL). Only its sha256 hex is stored in `Session`. The session is deleted on logout, password reset, role change and deactivation. AUTH_SECRET is required by env.ts but nothing uses it. Username login (b15f163) only relaxed the login validator to `^[a-z0-9._%+@-]{2,200}$`. The lookup is still `User.email`, so the "admin" account is a row with email='admin', created outside the repo (it is in neither seed.ts nor install.sh). There are 5 roles (SUPER/ORG/KINDERGARTEN_ADMIN, TEACHER, PARENT) on an Organization→Kindergarten→Class tenant model. Every service calls authorizeChild/authorizeGoal/authorizeContent in src/lib/permissions/index.ts. These combine tenant scope with the record lookup in one query, so a foreign ID returns 404, and then apply a 7-action role matrix. Uploads cover family photos (with a consent model) and narration audio. They have a type allowlist, size caps, magic-byte sniffing and opaque keys, and are served only through authorized routes. AuditLog gets about 55 action types with primitive-only metadata from 48 call sites. Much of the rest is beyond the MVP spec: child device mode with a PIN, media consent and narration, multi-tenancy, email password reset, S3, analytics, notifications, weekly planner, and the profile attribute/confidence engine.

keep.item: bcrypt password hashes: keep them as they are so the existing admin password still works
keep.reason: bcryptjs 3.0.3 makes standard `$2b$12$` 60-char hashes from UTF-8 input (it emits `$2b$`, see node_modules/bcryptjs/index.js:96). The Python `bcrypt` package can verify these exactly, so stored hashes keep working after the move.
keep.how: Copy `User.passwordHash` into `users.password_hash` unchanged. In backend/app/security.py, `pip install bcrypt` (pyca, wheels for Python 3.12) and use `bcrypt.checkpw(pw.encode('utf-8')[:72], h.encode('ascii'))`; new hashes use `bcrypt.hashpw(pw.encode('utf-8')[:72], bcrypt.gensalt(12))`. The `[:72]` slice copies bcryptjs's silent truncation; without it pyca bcrypt 5.x throws ValueError. Do NOT use passlib: it is unmaintained and breaks with bcrypt>=4.1/5.0. argon2-cffi cannot verify bcrypt. Mark these endpoints `def`, not `async def`, so the ~250 ms bcrypt call runs in the threadpool.

Then confirm the hash parses with pyca bcrypt: run `bcrypt.checkpw(b'x', h)` in the venv and expect False, not an error.

add.item: nginx security hardening
add.reason: Next.js currently sends the CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and HSTS headers. Without Next, nginx has to send them. The X-Forwarded-For handling also needs fixing.
add.how: Use `add_header ... always` for the CSP (default-src 'self'; no unsafe-eval) and the other headers. For `location /api/`, set `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr` and `Cache-Control no-store`. Add `limit_req` for login, `client_max_body_size 10m`, and no public location for /var/www/kidsphere/uploads (or an `internal` one for X-Accel-Redirect).

add.item: Authorship stamping from the session
add.reason: Spec §12 requires recording who entered each piece of information (created_by on baselines, observations, content and feedback).
add.how: Services always set created_by=current_user.id and never read it from the request body (extra='forbid' prevents that). parent_perspective and teacher_perspective entries also store an `entered_by`/`entered_at` pair.

risks: The 'admin' username account is not created anywhere in git (not in seed.ts or install.sh). Its role, active flag and hash format must be checked in the live PostgreSQL before the migration. pyca bcrypt verifies $2a$/$2b$/$2y$ but not argon2 or other schemes.

bcryptjs silently truncates passwords past 72 UTF-8 bytes, while pyca bcrypt 5.x raises ValueError. Without the `[:72]` slice, long passwords (Arabic or Hebrew at roughly 36+ characters) that work today would fail or return 500.
passlib is a trap on Python 3.12 with current bcrypt, because its version probe and the 72-byte self-test break. Use `bcrypt` (or pwdlib) directly.

All running and testing happens on the Ubuntu server, since there is no local Python. Hash compatibility, pytest security scenarios and the migration must run there against a separate test database (PG 16) without touching production data.

The current production login rate limit can be bypassed by spoofing X-Forwarded-For. The dummy-hash timing check also does nothing (62-char string, so bcryptjs returns immediately), which allows user enumeration through response time. Neither bug should be carried into the port.

The main regression risk is losing the scope-in-the-same-query / 404 discipline when hand-writing SQLAlchemy queries. Port tests/integration/security.test.ts scenarios as pytest before building features.

bcrypt cost 12 takes about 250 ms of CPU per login on 2 vCPUs and blocks the event loop inside `async def`. Use sync endpoints or run_in_threadpool, and run 1–2 uvicorn workers given about 1.4 GB of free RAM.
Switching session stores logs everyone out at cutover. Reusing the cookie name `ks_session` is safe only if old tokens simply fail the lookup.

Spec §17 now allows recent observations in AI prompts, which reverses the current PRIVACY.md rule. Observation text must be scrubbed of other children's and family names, and health answers must stay excluded.
Production may already have password-reset links in journald from the dev mail transport. They expire after an hour, so the remaining risk is low, but the transport must not be ported.

summary: The AI layer (src/lib/ai/*) has three providers: Anthropic (claude-opus-5-5 through beta.messages with server-side fallback, effort medium and JSON-schema output), OpenAI (gpt-5) and a deterministic trilingual DEMO provider. A shared pipeline calls the model, validates with Zod plus childSafetyIssues (a banned-term list in en/ar/he, a link regex and story-graph checks), repairs once, then fails safely. Generation is goal-driven only. The data-minimizing context builder (src/server/services/generation-context.ts) sends display name, age band, the goal and at most 2 interests, 2 strengths, 3 supports and 3 avoid items. It never sends observations. Output is one of 4 "kinds" (story with branching scenes, routine, activity with isPreferred rounds, adult guide) mapped from 12 Prisma ContentTypes. These are rendered by a dependency-light child player (src/features/player/content-player.tsx) inside a PIN-locked child mode. Around this sits a large engine: a 5-state approval workflow, versions, templates, narration, character consent, a regenerate dialog with 6 modes, a 5-day weekly-plan generator, an AI attribute-suggestion op, a ProfileAttribute evidence/confidence engine (REPORTED/OBSERVED/CORROBORATED), a count-based "professional team" concern flag and an analytics event store. The DEMO provider is disabled in production (ALLOW_DEMO_AI_IN_PRODUCTION=false). With no API key on the Ubuntu server, AI generation on kids.kortexd.com currently throws AI_UNAVAILABLE. Against the spec, the following conflict: there is no Strength Builder mode, no spec-18 output shapes, no video plan, and no match_pairs/sequence/categorize renderers. "MATCHING_ACTIVITY" is a label only and renders as multiple choice. There are quantitative ratio displays, clinical-adjacent domain labels and a banned-term list that blocks "problem" (which breaks the Maya story-creation example).

add.item: Python dependencies and config
add.reason: The new backend needs explicit pins. The current .env.example sets ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 while the code default is claude-opus-5-5, which is inconsistent.
add.how: Add anthropic (1.x; it requires Python >=3.10 and uses httpx2) and pydantic>=2 to requirements.txt. In .env.example set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= (empty -> templates), ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 and AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60. Set nginx proxy_read_timeout 120s for /api/children/*/content/generate.

risks: No API key on the server: the Claude path cannot be exercised end-to-end in production until a key is added. The template provider must be the tested default, and the Claude code must be covered by pytest with a fake client. Pytest only runs on the Ubuntu server venv because there is no local Python.

Synchronous generation without a queue (spec bans Celery/Redis): an Opus 5.5 call with effort medium and max_tokens 16000 can take 20-60 s, and a pack call longer. Use timeout=60 and max_retries=1, a 120 s nginx proxy_read_timeout, a UI spinner, and fall back to templates on timeout. Run uvicorn with 2 workers given ~1.4 GB RAM and 2 CPUs.

The structured-outputs schema subset: Pydantic model_json_schema() emits $defs, title, default, anyOf for Optional and length constraints. Without the ported sanitizer, requests can 400. Discriminated unions (GameOut) should be tested against the API once a key exists.

Banned-term false positives and negatives in ar/he: substring matching with Hebrew/Arabic prefixes can block normal words or miss inflections. The current 'problem' ban already conflicts with spec example 45 and the 'Problem solving' strength. Expect iteration on the allowlist.

Arabic/Hebrew grammatical gender: the demo heroes are deliberately masculine so templates agree, but sentences addressing the child by name need gender agreement and gender is optional (spec 5). Use gender-neutral phrasing or branch on gender when set.

Privacy regression: adding observations to the AI context (spec 17) moves teacher free text to an external provider. The masking is name-based only, so other identifying details in the text can leak. Keep the ≤5 observation and 300-char caps and never send parent-sensitive answers.

Content shape migration: existing contentVersion.body JSON (scenes/rounds/steps/kind) will not validate against the new spec shapes. Either write a one-off converter for existing approved content or archive it during the DB migration.

Dropping the confidence/evidence engine loses automatic corroboration logic. Baseline validation (spec 24) then depends on AI or template suggestions plus teacher judgement, so the 'never claim certainty from 1-2 observations' rule must be enforced in both prompt and template (e.g. force needs_more_observation when count < 3).

area: User interface, design system, i18n, RTL (src/app pages, src/components, UI parts of src/features, src/lib/i18n, globals.css, src/lib/client)
summary: The UI is about 50 App Router pages (around 2,900 lines) and 30 feature client components (around 4,200 lines) on top of 12 small UI/layout primitives (around 830 lines). Every page is an async Server Component that reads Prisma and the session directly (requirePageActor, getI18n, db.*). So no page file can be reused as-is; each needs a client-side fetch against FastAPI. The JSX markup can be kept. Most primitives are plain React with Tailwind. Only button.tsx (ButtonLink), misc.tsx (PageHeader back link, TabNav), app-shell.tsx, locale-switcher.tsx and notifications-bell.tsx import next/link or next/navigation. 16 of the 30 feature components import next/navigation, almost only useRouter().push/refresh. All @prisma/client imports in client code are type-only. RTL is done properly. The server sets <html lang dir> from a cookie or the user's language (default ar). The CSS uses only logical utilities (ms/me/ps/pe/start/end/border-s/border-e, text-start); the only physical class is -space-x-3, which is paired with rtl:space-x-reverse. Directional icons flip with rtl:rotate-180. User and AI text uses dir="auto", and email/password/PIN fields use dir="ltr". The content player takes its direction from the content's language, not the UI language. i18n is a small home-made typed system with no library. There are 3 TS object dictionaries (en.ts is the key set; ar/he are typed as Messages so TypeScript enforces matching keys), each with about 695 string leaves (en 32 KB, ar 42 KB, he 38 KB) and {var} placeholders, plus separate three-language domain label sets (vocabulary.ts has 120 entries with emoji; observations/definition.ts; questionnaires/definition.ts has 14 sections). Several existing screens are already close to the spec: the child overview is close to the child profile, quick observation to quick observation, the parent questionnaire wizard to the Add Child wizard engine, the content review/player to preview/approve, the record-outcome dialog to feedback, and admin SimpleFormDialog+Table to user/class management. The rest is extra scope (child PIN mode, class weekly planner, library/templates, photo consent characters, multi-tenant admin, notifications).

add.item: Plural-aware messages and an age formatter
add.reason: The translator only supports {n} substitution ('{n} years'). Arabic has 6 plural categories and Hebrew has dual forms. The spec wants '4 years 2 months'.
add.how: Add plural keys (e.g. years_one/years_two/years_few/years_many/years_other) chosen through Intl.PluralRules(locale). Add formatAge(dob, locale).

add.item: New dictionary keys and spec terminology
add.reason: New screens (wizard steps, baseline/current understanding, development review, feedback, game templates) need copy in 3 languages, using the spec's vocabulary (Strengths, Growth Area, Current Focus, Area for Support).
add.how: Extend the existing nested TS dictionaries; the Messages type forces ar and he to match. Have an Arabic and a Hebrew speaker review the strings.

add.item: Mobile quick-add entry point
add.reason: Spec §37: Add Observation especially on mobile.
add.how: Teacher phone layout gets the parent-style bottom bar (Children, ＋ Observation, Content, Account). The centre ＋ opens a child picker and then the quick observation.

add.item: Nginx config for the SPA
add.reason: Static SPA routing and /api proxy (spec §47).
add.how: root /var/www/kidsphere/frontend; location / { try_files $uri /index.html; }. Hashed /assets/ get long-cache immutable; index.html gets no-cache. location /api/ proxies to uvicorn. Serve uploads only through an authenticated FastAPI endpoint (optionally X-Accel-Redirect).

risks: Porting cost sits in data loading, not markup. All ~50 pages are Server Components that call Prisma services and requirePageActor directly, so every screen needs a FastAPI endpoint plus client fetch, loading and error states. The UI also uses Prisma model shapes (displayName, avatarColor, primaryLanguage, attribute confidence) that change under the spec's schema.
Without SSR, <html dir> is not known at first paint. If the inline dir/lang bootstrap script in index.html is skipped, Arabic and Hebrew users see an LTR flash and layout jump on every load.

format.ts uses 'ar-EG', which renders Arabic-Indic digits (٤) for dates and ages, while Hebrew and English use Western digits. The product owner should decide (e.g. 'ar-u-nu-latn') before building the date/number-heavy timeline.
The translator has no plural support. Arabic and Hebrew strings with {n} are grammatically wrong for some counts, and the spec's '4 years 2 months' needs proper plural forms.

Labels live in two places: UI dictionaries and three-language L objects in TS domain files. Python needs the same keys for validation and AI prompts. Without one shared vocab.json the frontend, backend and AI prompts will drift.

Dictionary enum keys are UPPER_CASE Prisma enums (DRAFT, TEACHER_REVIEW, HELPED…) while the spec uses lowercase values (draft, worked_well…). The renames touch all 3 files and every t(`enums.…`) call; unreviewed leftovers fall back to raw keys silently.

Some copy is semi-clinical or jargon for teachers ('Executive function', 'Attention & executive function', TRIGGER shown as 'Things to avoid', 'Corroborated'). It needs a terminology pass against spec §2.

Drag-style game templates (match_pairs, sequence, categorize) do not exist and are the hardest RTL and touch work. Sequence order and swipe direction must follow content dir, which the current player already gets via dirOf(body.language).

Everything is built and tested on the server: there is no local Node or Python run, per the user. Vite builds are light, but running the old Next service, a Vite build and uvicorn side by side on 2 CPUs with about 1.4GB free RAM may hit memory limits. Playwright browsers are heavy, so e2e on that server should be minimal or skipped.

There is no API key, so generated content will come from the demo/offline path. The UI must keep a clear DEMO badge (common.demo / demoHint exist) so teachers don't mistake template output for personalized AI output.

Session handling moves from server redirects to client guards. FastAPI must set an HttpOnly same-site cookie behind the same Nginx origin so api()'s credentials:'same-origin' keeps working. Add CSRF protection for state-changing calls.

summary: This area is built for a single Next.js 16 standalone server. Each deploy runs `git archive HEAD`, sends it over SSH with deploy/remote-deploy.sh (Windows calls it through deploy/deploy-kids.ps1), then deploy/deploy.sh on the server runs npm ci, `prisma migrate deploy` and `next build`. kidsphere.service runs `node .next/standalone/server.js` on 127.0.0.1:3070, and nginx proxies all traffic to it, including /_next/static. The live server names are /opt/kidsphere-app, user kidsphere-app, service kidsphere-app, DB kidsphere_app, storage /var/lib/kidsphere-app/storage, and a private Node at /opt/kidsphere-node. The existing certbot certificate for kids.kortexd.com is reused. Local development assumed an embedded Postgres (scripts/db-server.mjs on :5433) or docker-compose.yml, Vitest for unit tests and real-DB integration tests, and Playwright e2e against `next dev` on :3100. The user says "we deploy on ubuntu no local", so every local build and run path is obsolete. That covers BUILD_LOCALLY, embedded PG, Docker and .claude/launch.json. All builds and tests must run on the Ubuntu server. The reusable parts are the provisioning logic, the TLS and nginx takeover logic, the git-archive deploy flow, the systemd hardening, the CSP headers and the test scenarios. kortex-messaging runs on the same host (185.229.226.37) and already deploys a FastAPI + Vite SPA behind nginx, so it is a proven reference. All 7 top-level docs (README, ARCHITECTURE, DECISIONS, ROADMAP, PRIVACY, AGENTS, CLAUDE) describe Next/Prisma/multi-tenant/child-mode and must be rewritten.

simplify.reason: Removing Prisma, the standalone build and the Next build shrinks the script and its memory use. The Next build needed `--max-old-space-size=1536`; a Vite build of a small SPA needs far less.
simplify.how: Steps: 1) pip install, gated by the requirements.txt hash. 2) Optionally run deploy/run-tests.sh (RUN_TESTS=1) and abort the deploy on failure. 3) pg_dump kidsphere_app to /var/backups/kidsphere/. 4) `venv/bin/alembic upgrade head`. 5) In frontend/: hash-gated `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck && npm run build -- --outDir dist.new`, then swap dist.new into dist. 6) `systemctl restart kidsphere-api`, then the health loop. 7) `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx` only if the config changed.

simplify.reason: `set -a && . ./.env` runs .env as shell code and breaks on unquoted values; kortex-messaging needed a Python re-quoting workaround for the same problem. Backend vars in the environment can also leak into the Vite build.

Run the frontend build with a clean environment (`env -i PATH=... npm run build`); the API base is always the relative /api. Rewrite backend/.env.example with: DATABASE_URL (postgresql+psycopg://kidsphere_app:...@localhost:5432/kidsphere_app), TEST_DATABASE_URL (…/kidsphere_app_test), SECRET_KEY, COOKIE_SECURE=true, UPLOAD_DIR=/var/www/kidsphere/uploads, AI_PROVIDER (anthropic|openai|demo), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL, ALLOW_DEMO_AI_IN_PRODUCTION, DEFAULT_LOCALE=ar, VIDEO_PROVIDER=none. Drop STORAGE_DRIVER, S3_* and the :5433 URLs.

add.item: Cutover runbook from the Next deployment
add.reason: The live server still runs kidsphere-app (Next) on :3070 against a Prisma-shaped kidsphere_app DB. install.sh's port guard aborts if another service holds the port.
add.how: Document and script it: stop and disable kidsphere-app; pg_dump the old DB; either `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public AUTHORIZATION kidsphere_app;` (it holds only demo data, so confirm with the PO first) or keep it and point the new app at a fresh DB; create kidsphere_app_test; create /var/www/kidsphere/uploads (owner kidsphere-app, mode 750); run install.sh with SERVICE=kidsphere-api, APP_USER=kidsphere-app, DB_NAME=kidsphere_app, PORT=3070; reuse the existing certificate.

risks: Port 3070 and the server_name are held by the running kidsphere-app (Next) service. install.sh's port check aborts unless that service is stopped first, so the cutover order matters.

The existing kidsphere_app DB contains Prisma tables and _prisma_migrations, so Alembic must not run against it unchanged. Take a backup and then drop/recreate the schema or use a new DB. Confirm with the PO that only demo data is there.

git archive extraction over a live directory leaves deleted files behind, e.g. an old Alembic revision giving multiple heads or stale Python modules. Extract to a release directory and rsync --delete, excluding venv, .env and node_modules.
Vite empties outDir at build start, so building straight into the nginx root takes the site down for the whole build. Build to dist.new or /tmp, then swap.

All tests run on the production host because there is no local Python. That host also runs kortex-messaging (gunicorn with 4 workers, Celery, Redis) and has about 1.4 GB free. Run pytest and the Vite build one after the other, cap NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=768, and run as kidsphere-app, never root.
A misconfigured TEST_DATABASE_URL could make the TRUNCATE fixture wipe live data. Make the `_test` name guard mandatory in conftest, and keep the test DB name separate from DB_NAME in install.sh.

No AI key is configured. Tests and the demo must force a deterministic offline provider. Production needs an explicit ALLOW_DEMO_AI_IN_PRODUCTION flag (same pattern as today), or generation endpoints must fail clearly.

nginx 1.24: do not copy `http2 on;` from the kortex-messaging config (that directive needs 1.25.1+); keep `listen 443 ssl http2`. nginx drops server-level add_header lines in any location that sets its own, so include the security headers snippet in every location.

Uploads live under /var/www/kidsphere/uploads, next to the web root. Never add an nginx location that exposes that directory directly; serve uploads only through an authenticated FastAPI route or X-Accel-Redirect. Set permissions to kidsphere-app, mode 750.
In-process rate limiting and any in-memory session state are only correct with a single uvicorn worker. Keep --workers 1, or move that state into PostgreSQL.
Without local Python or Node runs, mistakes only show up on the server. The deploy must be gated on run-tests.sh, and TESTS_ONLY=1 should be the habitual pre-deploy step.
The current TLS template hard-codes `kidsphere-app.*.log` names. The new service name must be templated, or logs will mix with the old site's during the transition.

area: Content plan: mapping the PO's two Hebrew source documents onto wizard steps 1-7, quick observations, feedback and development review
summary: The two documents overlap heavily with SPEC sections 5-11 and with content the current app already has. The parents intake (57 questions, already live as kidsphere-parents-intake-he-v1 in C:\projects\survey-src\src\lib\parents-content.ts) is a longer version of steps 2-7. The observation model is a roughly 90-item, 3-level professional rating form, so it cannot go into the wizard without breaking the 5-7 minute budget. My recommendation: the wizard takes the parents intake's multiple-choice lists, reduced to the SPEC lists. From the observation model it takes only cheap pieces: the 3-level support scale, the daily-routine stages as observation 'context', the 11 need-focus categories mapped onto SPEC's 11 priority categories, the 5-stage observation model as optional collapsed fields on an observation, 'what have we already tried / what helped' as optional focus-area details, and the משמעותי/חלקי/ללא שינוי review scale mapped to SPEC section 25. The per-item domain grids (§1-§11) are not imported; that knowledge builds up through quick observations instead. Most option labels already exist in en/ar/he in src/features/child-understanding/vocabulary.ts, src/features/questionnaires/definition.ts and src/features/observations/definition.ts (CONTEXTS matches the model's daily-routine stages exactly). They can be exported to one JSON options file used by both FastAPI and React, with key renames to SPEC wording; new labels are listed per item. One support_level enum (independent / some_support / significant_support / not_observed) should be used in Step 5, quick observations and content feedback. SPEC currently uses three different scales, and without one shared scale the 'compare against baseline' step does not work. Several source terms need neutral replacements (קשב וריכוז, ויסות חושי, התנהגות as a category, מדד הצלחה, הפניה, מתפרץ, מתקשה מאוד, קושי); these are flagged below. Estimated time is about 5.5-6.5 minutes per role, with parent and teacher each seeing only their own fields.

add.how: PARENT: parent_priorities, multi from focus_categories: emotional, social, language, communication, independence, attention, motor, learning, transitions, confidence, other, plus note. From the model, with existing labels in DOMAIN_ITEMS: calming_after_frustration (emotional, calms_after_frustration), separating_in_the_morning (transitions, separation), sharing_toys (social, shares), following_two_step_instructions (language, multi_step_instructions), coping_with_mistakes (confidence, handles_mistakes), telling_about_an_experience (language, recounts). add.item: Neutral-wording replacement table (applied to labels, hints and AI prompts)
add.reason: SPEC section 2 forbidden vocabulary, plus SPEC section 11 'never weaknesses'. The source documents use several clinical or deficit terms.
add.how: קשב וריכוז / attention -> ריכוז והתמדה / Focus & persistence (the term is in FORBIDDEN_CHILD_TERMS and reads as ADHD). ויסות חושי / מוצף -> 'דברים בסביבה שמשפיעים' / 'כשזה יותר מדי' (not a clinical sensory profile). התנהגות as a need category -> removed; a concrete focus is named instead. מוקדי צורך / צרכים מרכזיים / קושי מרכזי -> מוקדי התמקדות / תחומים לתמיכה (Current Focus / Areas for Support). מה גורם לקושי -> מה נראה שמקשה. מדד הצלחה -> איך נדע שזה עוזר (descriptive). תוכנית התערבות / הערכה -> 'מה ננסה' / סקירת התפתחות (Development review). הפניה בהתאם לצורך / צוות רב-מקצועי -> 'שיחה עם הצוות החינוכי'. מתפרץ -> not an option (existing neutral label 'Big emotional reaction' / תגובה רגשית עוצמתית if needed). מתקשה מאוד -> זקוק/ה להרבה תמיכה. מתקשה להירגע / struggles -> לוקח זמן להירגע / Takes time to calm down. struggles with turn-taking -> Still learning to take turns. רמת תפקוד -> כמה תמיכה נדרשה. risks: Wizard length creep: the intake has 57 questions and the model has about 90 rated items. Unless optional fields stay collapsed and parent and teacher see only their own fields, the wizard goes past 5-7 minutes. Port the existing entrySeconds timing (quick-observation-form.tsx) to measure step durations.

SPEC defines three different support scales (section 9 four levels, section 20 No/Some/Significant, section 21 Independent/With support/Difficult). If they are stored separately, the 'compare against baseline' step cannot work. 'Difficult' mapped to significant_support is a slight change of meaning that the product owner should accept.

Key renames (vehicles->cars_transportation, building->construction, stories_books->stories, hard_to_calm->takes_time_to_calm, some_help->some_support, etc.) break any migrated production data unless a rename map is applied in the data migration.
The survey stores Hebrew labels, not keys. Any change to a label in parents-content.ts breaks the import map, and that file is marked LOCKED.

Arabic labels for NEW options have no source document (the product owner supplied Hebrew only). Some existing Arabic labels read as literal translations (e.g. 'إدخال الخيط' for threading). A native ar reviewer is needed before release. Hebrew teacher UI strings are currently feminine imperative (השתמשי, סמני) while option labels use slash forms; decide on one convention.
The safety_note (allergies/medical) field adds health data. It must be excluded from the AI context and staff-only, or dropped if the product owner prefers the minimal-data rule in SPEC section 35.
Gender is optional but grammatical gender in he/ar stories depends on it; content generation needs a neutral fallback when it is unspecified.
Focus titles stored as free localized text cannot be re-translated if the teacher changes UI language. Storing suggestion_key alongside title avoids this.

No local Python: validating options.json against Pydantic validators and running import scripts can only happen on the Ubuntu server. Keep options.json pure data so the React build and local Node tooling can lint it (forbidden terms, all three languages present) before deployment.
